# Patched upstream crates

Upstream crates Enclave builds with a change, each a copy of the released
crate with the smallest edit, marked `ENCLAVE PATCH` in the source. Each
change is offered upstream; the copy goes when a release carries it
(`docs/completion-plan.md` X10).

| Crate | Version | Licence | Used by | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nym-client-core` | 1.21.5 | Apache-2.0 | `nym/` workspace (`[patch.crates-io]`) | `MessageHandler::get_or_create_sender_tag` draws a fresh `AnonymousSenderTag` for every message instead of keeping one per recipient | One tag per recipient lets a server link every request a client sends it; Enclave requests must be unlinkable (`docs/09-transport.md` §1). Enclave sends every reply SURB a reply needs with its request, so no "more SURBs" request ever uses an old tag. |
| `nym-client-core` | 1.21.5 | Apache-2.0 | as above | New module `enclave`: a process-wide count of messages handed to the client and not yet prepared (`note_submitted`, settled by the input listener and the reply controller) plus fragments sent and not yet acknowledged (added in `MessageHandler::insert_pending_acks`, settled in `ActionController::handle_remove`); `outstanding()` reads it. Also: a gap between real packets with Poisson off (`set_packet_gap`, applied in `real_traffic_stream.rs::poll_immediate`), a runtime loop-cover mean (`set_loop_cover_delay`, read by `cover_traffic_stream.rs` for each loop packet), a count of fragments prepared (`fragments_sent`), and of real packets let out with the queue behind them (`packets_out`, `queued`) | A one-way send returns once the message is queued; a process that exits then loses it. `enclave-nym-sdk`'s `NymDriver::flush` waits for the count to reach 0 before nymd or the ingress exits (`docs/09-transport.md` §6.1). The pacing settings let a device pace a tick's packets evenly and change loop cover with its profile without rebuilding the client (`docs/09-transport.md` §6.3). Process-wide because each Enclave process runs one mixnet client. |
| `nym-client-core` | 1.21.5 | Apache-2.0 | as above | `tungstenite`/`tokio-tungstenite` 0.20 → 0.24 in `Cargo.toml` | 0.20 runs the gateway connection on rustls 0.21 and rustls-webpki 0.101 (RUSTSEC-2026-0098, -0099, -0104); 0.24 is on rustls 0.23. No source change was needed. |
| `nym-gateway-client` | 1.21.5 | Apache-2.0 | `nym/` workspace | the same version bump | the same |
| `nym-gateway-client` | 1.21.5 | Apache-2.0 | as above | `client::set_stream_connector`: a process-wide connector that, when set, opens every gateway connection (`websockets.rs::connect_async_inner`) instead of the local DNS lookup and TCP connect; the WebSocket and TLS then run over the stream it returns | A device reaches its entry gateway only through Tor (`enclave-tord`'s SOCKS5 port), so the gateway never sees its address and nothing is resolved locally (`docs/09-transport.md` §1). nym-sdk's `custom_gateway_transceiver` can't do this: it requires a custom gateway registration and skips authentication. |
| `nym-gateway-requests` | 1.21.5 | Apache-2.0 | `nym/` workspace | the same version bump | the same |
| `ptrs` | 0.1.0 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | main workspace (`enclave-tord` through `obfs4`; `[patch.crates-io]`) | `helpers::make_state_dir` sets the owner-only mode on Unix only (`cfg(unix)` on the `DirBuilderExt` import and the `mode` call); the library is built as an rlib only (upstream adds a cdylib) | The crate didn't compile on Windows; Enclave never calls this function (it runs obfs4 in-process, not as a managed transport). A cdylib's unhashed file names collided between builds sharing a target directory (E0460). |

| `libsqlite3-sys` | 0.30.1 | MIT | `nym/` workspace (`[patch.crates-io]`, `third_party/libsqlite3-sys-030`) | Not a copy: a crate named `libsqlite3-sys` 0.30.1 whose library re-exports 0.37.0, with 0.30's features forwarded | sqlx 0.8 (nym-sdk's storage) asks for 0.30 and rusqlite 0.39 (arti) for 0.37, and both declare `links = "sqlite3"`, so cargo can't build them into one program. Android and iOS run Tor and the Nym client in the app's one process (`nym/enclave-mobile`), which needs one SQLite. sqlx builds and runs on the 0.37 bindings (the nym tests and the local-mixnet round trip, which uses the persistent stores, pass). |

Every other `nym-*` crate is pinned to 1.21.5 in `nym/Cargo.lock`: mixing
1.21.5 with the later-published 1.22.0 helper crates doesn't compile.
| `nym-gateway-client` | 1.21.5 | Apache-2.0 | as above | `client::tickets_spent()`: a process-wide count of zk-nym tickets claimed with gateways (and of tickets a gateway reported as already spent) in `claim_bandwidth` | A device's client keeps its ticketbooks in memory; the vault records how many were spent and imports only the unspent range at the next connection, or the gateway would see the same tickets again (`docs/09-transport.md` §7). |
| `nym-credential-storage` | 1.21.5 | Apache-2.0 | as above | The in-memory backend keeps ticketbooks in a `BTreeMap` by id instead of a `HashMap` | Tickets are then spent from ticketbooks in import order, so a count of tickets spent says which ones are gone. |
